# Hawiyat Kit

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude)
[![CI Status](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/Hawiyat-Org/hawiyat-kit/ci.yml?branch=main)](https://github.com/Hawiyat-Org/hawiyat-kit/actions)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude)](LICENSE)

One-command setup for **Claude Code**, **OpenCode**, **pi**, **DeepSeek
Harness**, **Codex**, and **Claude Desktop** with Hawiyat's LLM provider.
Smart backup, auth, merge, uninstall, and rollback with minimal runtime
dependencies.

The repository is `hawiyat-kit`. The npm package remains
`@hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude`, and the binary remains `hawiyat-claude`;
`hawiyat` is an alias.

## Quickstart

```bash
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude install --token <your-hawiyat-token>
```

That's it. After running this command, `claude` sessions will transparently
use Hawiyat's API for all inference.

## About

[Hawiyat](https://hawiyat.cloud) is a managed LLM inference provider.
Hawiyat Kit is the official installer that configures Claude Code to use
Hawiyat as its backend. It writes the required environment variables into
Claude Code's `settings.json` (which Claude Code natively supports since
v2.1.143), installs optional plugins, and sets up OpenCode with the
Hawiyat-ai provider — all without touching your shell rc files.

Every write is preceded by a timestamped backup. Every operation is
reversible. Nothing is global.

## Prerequisites

- **Node.js >= 20** (LTS). Check with `node --version`.
- **Claude Code CLI** installed and available in your `PATH`. Install from
  [code.anthropic.com](https://code.anthropic.com).
- **A Hawiyat API token** — sign up at [hawiyat.cloud](https://hawiyat.cloud)
  to get one.

## Installation

No global install required. Run directly via `npx`:

```bash
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude install --token sk-...
```

The published package ships the compiled `dist/` output, so users do not
need TypeScript or a build step. The first run may prompt you to confirm
overwriting existing `ANTHROPIC_*` env vars if they differ from Hawiyat's
defaults.

The package installs two equivalent binaries: `hawiyat` and
`hawiyat-claude`. Every example below works with either name.

## Supported harnesses

| Harness | Flag | Files written |
|---------|------|---------------|
| Claude Code | default (`claude`) | `~/.claude/settings.json` |
| OpenCode V1 / V2 | default (`opencode`) | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/opencode.json`); the schema follows the installed `opencode --version`. V2 uses the extension, V1 the raw provider |
| pi | `--pi` / `--targets pi` | `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`, `settings.json` with the extension; `models.json` with `--no-extensions` |
| DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) | `--deepseek` / `--targets deepseek` | `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`, `~/.dsh/.env` |
| Codex CLI | `--codex` / `--targets codex` | `~/.codex/config.toml`, `auth.json`, model catalog |
| Codex Desktop | `--codex-desktop` (Windows and macOS) | Same files as Codex CLI |
| Claude Desktop (Chat, Cowork, and Code) | `--claude-desktop` / `--targets claude-desktop` | `~/Library/Application Support/Claude-3p/configLibrary/`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Claude-3p\configLibrary\`, or `~/.config/Claude-3p/configLibrary/` |

## Commands

### showcase

Print an animated tour of the login and install commands. It is static in a
pipe, with `NO_COLOR`, or with `--no-animations`:

```bash
hawiyat showcase
hawiyat showcase --no-animations
NO_ANIMATIONS=1 hawiyat showcase
```

### install

Configure Claude Code and OpenCode for the Hawiyat provider.

| Flag                    | Description                                            | Default                    |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| `--token, -t <token>`  | Hawiyat API token (prompts if omitted)                 | —                          |
| `--full, -f`           | Full setup: env vars + superpowers plugin              | `false`                    |
| `--base-url <url>`     | Custom API base URL                                    | `https://ai.hawiyat.cloud` |
| `--model <model>`      | Model name to use                                      | `hawiyat-composer`         |
| `--no-opencode`        | Skip writing OpenCode provider config                  | `false`                    |
| `--force`              | Overwrite existing non-Hawiyat values without prompting | `false`                    |
| `--yes, -y`            | Skip all prompts (non-interactive mode)                | `false`                    |
| `--debug`              | Verbose output with stack traces                       | `false`                    |
| `--project`            | Write to project-local .claude/ instead of ~/.claude/  | `false`                    |
| `--codex`              | Configure Codex CLI only (skips Claude Code and OpenCode) | `false`                    |
| `--codex-desktop`      | Configure Codex Desktop (Windows and macOS; same files as `--codex`) | `false` |
| `--claude-desktop`     | Configure Claude Desktop 3P inference (local profile plus import fallback) | `false`                   |
| `--interactive, -i`    | Pick harnesses from a TTY menu                          | `false`                    |
| `--no-tui`             | Use the numeric menu instead of the arrow-key TUI      | `false`                    |
| `--targets <list>`     | Comma-separated targets: `claude,opencode,pi,deepseek,codex,claude-desktop` | `claude,opencode`          |
| `--pi`                 | Configure pi only                                       | `false`                    |
| `--deepseek`           | Configure DeepSeek Harness only                         | `false`                    |
| `--models <a,b,c>`     | Models to expose (Codex picker, pi, dsh, OpenCode)       | gateway discovery          |
| `--self-test`          | Run install in a temp HOME, assert the output, clean up. Requires `--token` | `false`                    |
| `--extensions`         | Install the official Hawiyat extension for pi/OpenCode | auto                       |
| `--no-extensions`      | Write the raw provider config; skip the extension      | auto                       |

## Extensions

pi and OpenCode have official Hawiyat extensions. Both are distributed from
GitHub, not npm, so the installer uses each harness's git install command.

| Harness | Repository | Install command | What it adds |
|---------|------------|-----------------|--------------|
| pi | <https://github.com/Hawiyat-Org/hawiyat-pi-extension> | `pi install git:github.com/Hawiyat-Org/hawiyat-pi-extension` | Provider `hawiyat`, `/stats`, `web_fetch`, subagents |
| OpenCode v2+ | <https://github.com/Hawiyat-Org/opencode-extension> | `opencode plugin add github:Hawiyat-Org/opencode-extension` | Package `@hawiyat/opencode-extension`; provider `hawiyat`, `/stats`, `usage_stats`, `webfetch`, subagents |

`install` defaults to `auto`: it installs the extension when the harness
binary is present and falls back to the raw provider config on any failure
(missing binary or a non-zero install). `--extensions` requires the extension
and exits 2 with the reason when the install fails, so scripts can catch it.
`--no-extensions` always writes the raw provider config and is the path for
offline or pinned setups.

The pi extension reads the key from `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`
(`hawiyat.key`); the installer does not copy it into `models.json`. The
OpenCode extension is v2 only: v1 keeps the raw `provider` block and never
runs `opencode plugin add`. A fresh OpenCode extension install writes the
plugin entry with `options.apiKey` and leaves `providers['hawiyat-ai']`
alone if an older raw install already created it.

### Interactive setup

Run `install` with no arguments on a terminal, or pass `--interactive`:

```bash
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude install --interactive

# Equivalent, using the short bin alias
hawiyat install -i
```

The menu is an arrow-key picker (Claude Code, OpenCode, pi, DeepSeek
Harness, Codex, Claude Desktop), followed by the token and whether Hawiyat
should become the default model where the harness supports it.
Non-interactive scripts should use `--targets` instead; `--interactive` exits
2 when stdin is not a TTY.

```text
  Hawiyat Kit
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  ⠋ Configure which harnesses?

  ❯ ◉ Claude Code        Anthropic CLI
    ◉ OpenCode           sst/opencode
    ◯ pi                 earendil-works/pi
    ◯ DeepSeek Harness   dsh
    ◯ Codex              CLI or Desktop (Windows/macOS)
    ◯ Claude Desktop     Chat, Cowork, and Code

  ↑/↓ move   space toggle   a all   enter confirm   esc cancel
```

`↑`/`↓` (or `j`/`k`) move, space toggles, `a` selects all or none, Enter
confirms, and Esc, `q`, or Ctrl-C cancels. Claude Code and OpenCode are
selected by default.

Pass `--no-tui`, or set `NO_TUI=1`, to keep the numeric menu:

```bash
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude install --interactive --no-tui
NO_TUI=1 npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude install -i
```

```bash
# A few file-based harnesses in one run
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude install --targets claude,opencode,pi --token sk-...

# Claude Code, Codex, and Claude Desktop in one transaction
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude install --targets claude,codex,claude-desktop --token sk-...

# Just pi
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude install --pi --token sk-...

# Just DeepSeek Harness
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude install --deepseek --token sk-...
```

`--targets` cannot be combined with `--pi`, `--deepseek`, `--codex`,
`--codex-desktop`, or `--claude-desktop`; the CLI exits 2 with a clear
message. Restart pi (`pi`), OpenCode, or `dsh web` after a write so each
harness reloads its config.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning                                                              |
|------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0    | Success (already configured)                                         |
| 1    | Generic error, including `auth status` with no stored key            |
| 2    | Invalid input: unknown target, missing token, bad flag value         |
| 3    | Permission denied                                                    |
| 4    | Partial failure with auto-rollback, or no device endpoints on the dashboard |
| 5    | Unchanged: already configured or logged out, nothing written         |
| 6    | Backup failure                                                       |
| 7    | Invalid JSON in a file the CLI must parse                            |

### uninstall

Remove Hawiyat configuration.

| Flag             | Description                                                   |
|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--purge, -p`    | Remove only Hawiyat-managed keys from live files (no backup)  |
| `--debug`        | Verbose output with stack traces                              |

Default (no `--purge`): restores the most recent backup of each modified
file. If no backup is found, you must use `--purge`.

`--purge` removes the Hawiyat entries from Claude Code settings, the
OpenCode provider (both the V1 `provider` and V2 `providers` schema), the
pi providers/credentials/defaults, and the DeepSeek Harness route. Other
providers, credentials, and env lines are preserved. A `--project` purge
does not touch the home-scoped pi and dsh agent directories.

### update

Apply manifest deltas when the package version changes.

```bash
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude update
```

Updates `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to current package
defaults while preserving your existing `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`.

### rollback

Restore from a timestamped backup.

| Flag                     | Description                                    |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| `--list, -l`             | List available backups with timestamps and SHA |
| `--to <timestamp>`       | Restore a specific backup by timestamp         |
| `--dry-run`              | Preview what would be restored without writing |
| `--debug`                | Verbose output with stack traces               |

```bash
# See available backups
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude rollback --list

# Restore from a specific backup
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude rollback --to 20260601-120000

# Preview a rollback
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude rollback --dry-run
```

## Full Setup

The `--full` flag extends the basic install with OpenCode provider
configuration and plugin installation.

### What `--full` installs

1. **Claude Code env vars** in `~/.claude/settings.json` — same as basic
   install
2. **OpenCode provider** `hawiyat-ai` in
   `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` — enables Hawiyat models inside
   OpenCode
3. **Superpowers plugin** `superpowers@claude-plugins-official` — adds
   advanced Claude Code capabilities (test-driven development workflows,
   code review, branch management, and more)

```bash
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude install --full --token sk-...
```

### What gets written

**`~/.claude/settings.json` (`env` block):**

```json
{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://ai.hawiyat.cloud",
    "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "sk-...",
    "ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "hawiyat-composer",
    "ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH": "true",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY": "1"
  }
}
```

**`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (`provider` block):**

```json
{
  "provider": {
    "hawiyat-ai": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "https://ai.hawiyat.cloud",
        "apiKey": "sk-..."
      }
    }
  }
}
```

All existing keys in both files are preserved. Only the Hawiyat-managed keys
are added or updated.

## Codex

Configure **Codex** (OpenAI's CLI) instead of Claude Code:

```bash
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude install --codex --token sk-...
```

Writes `~/.codex/config.toml` (hawiyat provider + `model =
"hawiyat-composer-codex"`) and `~/.codex/auth.json` (`OPENAI_API_KEY`). Add
`--project` to also write a project-local `.codex/config.toml` (model only).
Claude Code and OpenCode files are left untouched.

`--codex-desktop` writes the same files for the Codex Desktop app, which is
supported on Windows and macOS (`--codex-desktop` exits 2 on Linux; use
`--codex`). Codex can also be selected in a combined run with `--targets
claude,codex,claude-desktop`.

Multiple models are exposed in the Codex model picker via
`model_catalog_json`. By default the installer auto-discovers the models your
token can access from the Hawiyat gateway and falls back to
`hawiyat-composer-codex` + `hawiyat-astra` when offline. Customize with:

```bash
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude install --codex --token sk-... \
  --models "hawiyat-composer-codex,hawiyat-astra"   # or --no-discovery
```

Image generation is wired in natively: the installer writes a
`hawiyat-imagegen` skill to `~/.codex/skills/` that routes image
 generate/edit requests through the Hawiyat gateway (`gpt-image-2.5` by
default, `gpt-image-2` still selectable with `--model`) via a dependency-free
node runner. Ask Codex for an image and the skill handles
the rest (auth via `HAWIYAT_API_KEY`).

## Claude Desktop (Chat, Cowork, Code)

Claude Desktop does **not** read `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` or
`~/.claude/settings.json` for inference routing, and
`claude_desktop_config.json` only registers MCP servers. The supported
route is the app's third-party (3P) inference configuration.

```bash
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude install --claude-desktop --token sk-...
```

Or store the key once and skip `--token`:

```bash
hawiyat auth login --token sk-...
hawiyat install --claude-desktop --models claude-h-o55f
```

This writes the app's local 3P profile and selects it, then sets
`deploymentMode: "3p"` in the root `claude_desktop_config.json` files while
preserving the other keys:

- Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Claude-3p\configLibrary\<id>.json` and `_meta.json`
- macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude-3p/configLibrary/`
- Linux: `~/.config/Claude-3p/configLibrary/`

Relaunch Claude Desktop and pick a Hawiyat model. No import dialog is needed.
The same profile covers Chat, Cowork, and Code.

When the process can write `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude` (an elevated run),
the installer also writes the managed policy. A standard Windows user cannot
write that key, so the local profile is the normal path. If `HKLM` policy is
present, Windows ignores `HKCU`; the installer warns and keeps the import file.

### Bootstrap mode

If the dashboard serves the per-user configuration, write an OIDC anchor
instead of a static key:

```bash
hawiyat install --claude-desktop \
  --bootstrap-client-id <google-desktop-client-id> \
  --bootstrap-base-url https://dash-stg.hawiyat.cloud
```

No token is required. The app signs in with Google on launch, the dashboard
exchanges the code with the Google client secret, and the bootstrap response
returns the plan key and model list. The anchor contains no key:

```json
{
  "bootstrapUrl": "https://dash-stg.hawiyat.cloud/api/desktop/bootstrap",
  "bootstrapOidc": {
    "clientId": "<id>",
    "authorizationUrl": "https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth",
    "tokenUrl": "https://dash-stg.hawiyat.cloud/api/desktop/token",
    "scopes": "openid email profile",
    "redirectHost": "127.0.0.1"
  },
  "disableDeploymentModeChooser": true
}
```

The dashboard needs `GOOGLE_DESKTOP_CLIENT_ID` and
`GOOGLE_DESKTOP_CLIENT_SECRET`. See the dashboard's
`docs/desktop-bootstrap.md` for the route contract.

The route is staging-only today: `GET
https://dash.hawiyat.cloud/api/desktop/bootstrap` returns 404, while staging
answers 401 without a Google ID token. The public desktop client id is
`826004629271-cq6ufd5g61d8fd4ornrtv3macp641aub.apps.googleusercontent.com`;
the anchor carries it with the dashboard token URL and never a client secret.

Bootstrap mode gives the dashboard control of the connection and model list.
Claude Desktop shows those fields as read-only. That is the trade-off for
zero-touch key delivery and Google sign-in. To let users edit the connection
settings, use the static local profile instead:

```bash
hawiyat auth login --targets claude-desktop
# or, with an existing key:
hawiyat install --claude-desktop --token sk-...
```

Static mode writes the key and model list into the local 3P profile, so the
Settings screen stays editable. The key is then stored on the device. The
first model is `claude-opus-hawiyat-composer`, labelled **Hawiyat Composer**,
because Claude Desktop only accepts Anthropic-shaped route names. The alias
`hawiyat-composer` is rewritten to that route.

The import file remains as a fallback at
`~/.claude/hawiyat-claude-desktop.json` (on WSL,
`C:\Users\<you>\Downloads\hawiyat-claude-desktop.json`). Importing it replaces
the applied configuration, so export the current one first if you need a
rollback. The static local profile contains your API key; the bootstrap
profile contains no key. Backups go under `~/.claude/hawiyat-backups`.

## Log in

Log in with a browser instead of copying a key:

```bash
hawiyat auth login
hawiyat auth status
hawiyat auth logout
```

`auth login` prints the URL and a one-time code, and opens the URL in your
default browser (the `verification_uri_complete` form pre-fills the code when
the dashboard offers it):

```
Open this URL in your browser:
https://dash.hawiyat.cloud/device?code=ABCD-1234

Enter this code:
ABCD-1234

Waiting for authorization...
```

Pass `--no-browser` (or set `NO_BROWSER=1`) to skip opening the browser, for
example on a headless host. If the browser cannot be opened the CLI prints
`Could not open a browser. Open the URL above manually.` and keeps polling.

On WSL, the CLI uses `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command Start-Process` to
open the Windows default browser instead of `xdg-open`.

Approve the code in the dashboard. The CLI then writes the token, the
inference URL, and the model to `~/.claude/settings.json`.

After a successful login, a terminal session asks **Configure your harnesses
now?** and opens the harness picker with the key already stored. For scripts,
name the harnesses on the login command:

```bash
hawiyat auth login --targets claude,opencode,pi,deepseek,codex,claude-desktop
hawiyat auth login --targets claude,claude-desktop
```

The same setup is available as per-harness flags. This is the quickest path
for a single harness:

```bash
hawiyat auth login --claude-desktop
hawiyat auth login --claude --opencode
hawiyat auth login --pi
hawiyat auth login --deepseek
hawiyat auth login --codex
hawiyat auth login --codex-desktop
```

Use `-i` or `--interactive` to open the picker after login:

```bash
hawiyat auth login -i
```

`--interactive` cannot be combined with `--targets`, a target flag, or
`--install`. `--no-install` still logs in only.

For Claude Desktop, `--claude-desktop` writes the editable static profile. Use
`install --claude-desktop --bootstrap-client-id ...` when you want the
dashboard-managed bootstrap profile instead.

`--install` uses the default `claude,opencode` set. `--no-install` logs in and
stops, which keeps the old one-step behavior.

Device login requires the dashboard device endpoints. Production does not
serve them yet: in November 2026 `POST
https://dash.hawiyat.cloud/api/cli/device_authorization` returns 404, so the
command exits 4 and points at the token path, which works today:

```bash
hawiyat auth login --token sk-...
hawiyat auth login --token sk-... --base-url https://ai.hawiyat.cloud --model hawiyat-composer
```

The staging dashboard has the endpoints today:

```bash
HAWIYAT_AUTH_BASE_URL=https://dash-stg.hawiyat.cloud hawiyat auth login --targets claude,claude-desktop
```

`auth status` shows the base URL, model, and a masked token. `auth logout`
removes the Hawiyat keys from `settings.json`; add `--revoke` to revoke the
key on the dashboard first. Revocation is best effort: if the call fails the
CLI warns and clears the local settings anyway.

Once a key is stored, later installs reuse it automatically:
`hawiyat install --claude-desktop`, `--pi`, `--deepseek`, and `--targets`
all fall back to the stored `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` when `--token` and the
environment variable are absent.

## Updating

To update your Hawiyat Kit installation after upgrading the npm package:

```bash
npx @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude update
```

This compares the installed manifest version against the current package
version and applies safe deltas — URL defaults, model names, and any new
env vars that later versions introduce. Your token is preserved.

## Troubleshooting

### "Token not recognized" after install

1. Verify the token is present in `~/.claude/settings.json`:
   ```bash
   node -e "console.log(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(require('path').join(require('os').homedir(), '.claude', 'settings.json'), 'utf-8')).env?.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN?.slice(0, 8))"
   ```
2. Ensure Claude Code is **restarted** after installation. The env block is
   read at startup.
3. Check that your Hawiyat token is still valid at
   [hawiyat.cloud/account](https://hawiyat.cloud/account).

### Permission denied when writing settings

The installer needs write access to `~/.claude/`. If you encounter
permission errors:

- Ensure the `.claude` directory is owned by your user
- On Linux/macOS: `chown -R $(whoami) ~/.claude`
- On Windows: run the terminal as your normal user (not as administrator)

### "Another install in progress" error

This means a previous install was interrupted. Run the install again — it
will detect the stale lock and prompt you to recover.

### pi reports duplicate tool names

`pi` found both the official package and a local copy of the same extension.
The installer now skips the official package when it sees local
`pi-stats`, `web-fetch`, `pi-interactive-subagents`, or `hawiyat-provider`
folders. To switch to the official package, move those folders out of
`~/.pi/agent/extensions/` and re-run `hawiyat install --pi`.

### Codex rejects the model catalog

Codex 0.145.0 and later require `base_instructions` and
`supports_parallel_tool_calls` in every model entry. Upgrade to Hawiyat Kit
1.6.5 or later and re-run `hawiyat install --codex` to regenerate
`~/.codex/hawiyat-model-catalog.json`.

### WSL vs Native Windows

Hawiyat Kit uses `os.homedir()` to locate config files, which resolves
correctly on both WSL and native Windows PowerShell. However:

- **WSL** stores Claude Code, OpenCode, pi, and dsh configs under the Linux
  home directory (`/home/user/.claude/`), but the Claude Desktop profile goes
  to the Windows app data directory
  (`C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Claude-3p\configLibrary\`), which is where
  the Windows app reads it. Backups stay in the Linux
  `~/.claude/hawiyat-backups/`. If you also use Claude Code in native Windows,
  run the installer in **both** environments.
- **Native Windows** stores configs under the Windows home directory
  (`C:\Users\<you>\.claude\`). PowerShell is fully supported; cmd.exe is
  not supported in v1.

### Rollback says no backups found

If uninstall with `--purge` was previously run, backups are removed along
with the config. The manifest retains a reference but the files are gone.
You will need to reconfigure manually or re-install.

## Architecture

Hawiyat Kit is an npx-installable TypeScript CLI that compiles to plain
ESM in `dist/` and writes `ANTHROPIC_*` environment variables into Claude
Code's `settings.json` env block (natively supported since Claude Code
v2.1.143). It uses a smart-merge engine to preserve all user
customizations, a backup manager that keeps up to 5 timestamped copies per
file, and atomic writes for crash safety.

For detailed architecture documentation, see
[docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

# Security Policy

## Token Storage

Hawiyat Kit stores your API token (`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`) in
`~/.claude/settings.json` inside the `env` block. Claude Code natively reads
environment variables from this file since v2.1.143.

**This file is readable by any process on your system**, as is standard for
environment variable configurations. The token is never written to shell rc
files (`.bashrc`, `.zshrc`, etc.), never passed as a CLI argument to
subprocesses, and never logged or echoed in output.

### Recommendations for High-Security Environments

1. **Use a scoped token** — Generate a dedicated API token with minimal
   permissions rather than using your master API key.

2. **Use the environment variable directly** — Set `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` as
   an OS-level environment variable instead of using the installer's `--token`
   flag. The installer reads this var as a fallback:
   ```bash
   export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="sk-..."
   npx hawiyat-claude install
   ```

3. **Restrict file permissions** — On macOS and Linux, ensure the settings
   file is readable only by the owner:
   ```bash
   chmod 0600 ~/.claude/settings.json
   ```
   The installer sets this permission automatically on write.

4. **Audit installed plugins** — Review which plugins have access to the env
   block via `claude plugins list`. Only install plugins you trust.

### Telemetry

Telemetry is on by default and disabled with `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`. The `install`,
`uninstall`, `update`, and `rollback` commands send one PostHog event each
with the platform, the Node version, a SHA-256 hash of the token, and a random
install ID stored in `~/.claude/.hawiyat-telemetry-id`. The token itself,
keys, hosts, paths, and prompt text are never sent. `HAWIYAT_TELEMETRY_HOST`
overrides the collector host.

### What Hawiyat Kit Does NOT Do

- No postinstall hooks — the npm package has zero install scripts
- No shell rc modification — token lives only in `settings.json`
- No subprocess token leakage — `--token` is consumed by the CLI and stored
  directly; it is never forwarded to child processes
- No credential storage in `node_modules` — configuration is written to
  `~/.claude/`, not the npm package directory

### Backup Safety

Backups are stored in `~/.claude/hawiyat-backups/` and may contain the API
token from the time of backup. If you uninstall, consider removing this
directory if token confidentiality is a concern:

```bash
rm -rf ~/.claude/hawiyat-backups
```

# Architecture

## Overview

Hawiyat Kit is an npx-installable Node.js tool that configures Claude Code,
OpenCode, pi, DeepSeek Harness, Codex, and Claude Desktop to use Hawiyat's
LLM provider. It writes `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, and
`ANTHROPIC_MODEL` into Claude Code's settings file — no shell rc editing, no
environment profiles, no global state.

### Key Design Properties

- **TypeScript source, plain ESM output** — `src/*.ts` compiles with
  `tsc` to `dist/*.js` (ESM). Every feature uses Node.js built-in modules
  (`node:fs/promises`, `node:path`, `node:os`, `node:readline/promises`,
  `node:crypto`, `node:child_process`); `posthog-node` is the only runtime
  package.
- **Idempotent** — running the same install twice produces identical state.
- **Reversible** — every write is preceded by a backup; uninstall restores
  the pre-install state.
- **Safe** — atomic writes prevent corruption; conflict detection warns on
  unexpected values.

## How It Works

Claude Code natively supports an `env` block in `~/.claude/settings.json`
since v2.1.143. Variables under this block are read at startup and merged
into the process environment, taking effect regardless of how `claude` was
launched.

Hawiyat Kit writes the following env vars:

| Variable                                  | Purpose                                         |
|-------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`                      | Routes API calls to `https://ai.hawiyat.cloud`  |
| `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`                    | Hawiyat API token for authentication            |
| `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`                         | Default model (`hawiyat-composer`)              |
| `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH`                      | Required when using non-first-party API         |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY` | Populates model picker from gateway          |

### Why `settings.json`?

- **Native support** — Claude Code reads the `env` block directly since
  v2.1.143 (confirmed in official documentation and schema).
- **Platform agnostic** — `os.homedir()` resolves identically on macOS,
  Linux, and Windows. No shell-specific quoting, no profile detection.
- **Project scope vs user scope** — we write to the user-level
  `settings.json` (not `settings.local.json`) so the config applies to all
  projects. Project-level overrides remain possible via
  `settings.local.json`.
- **No shell rc pollution** — the token never touches `.bashrc`, `.zshrc`,
  or any shell profile.

## Key Technical Decisions

### TypeScript Build, Plain ESM

The package uses `"type": "module"`. Source lives in `src/*.ts` and is
compiled by `tsc` to `dist/*.js` before tests and publishing. The published
`bin` entries (`hawiyat` and `hawiyat-claude`) both point at `dist/cli.js`, so
users install compiled output and never need TypeScript. Imports keep the
`.js` extension (NodeNext resolution). All other functionality uses Node.js
built-in modules:

| Module                      | Used For                                |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| `node:fs/promises`          | File I/O, atomic writes                 |
| `node:path`                 | Path resolution, backup naming          |
| `node:os`                   | `homedir()`, platform detection         |
| `node:readline/promises`    | Interactive token prompt                |
| `node:crypto`               | SHA256 hashing for manifest integrity   |
| `node:child_process`        | `claude plugins install` subprocess     |
| `node:util`                 | `parseArgs` for CLI argument parsing    |

This minimizes supply-chain risk from npm transitive dependencies and
keeps installs fast. `typescript` and `@types/node` are dev dependencies
only; `posthog-node` was already shipped for telemetry.

### parseArgs CLI Router

The CLI uses Node.js built-in `parseArgs` (stable in Node 20) instead of
commander, citty, or yargs. This keeps the runtime dependency count at one
(`posthog-node`) while providing enough functionality for 6 commands with
3-8 options each.

Command dispatch is a simple mapping:

```
install   → dist/commands/install.js  (src/commands/install.ts)
uninstall → dist/commands/uninstall.js (src/commands/uninstall.ts)
update    → dist/commands/update.js    (src/commands/update.ts)
rollback  → dist/commands/rollback.js  (src/commands/rollback.ts)
auth      → dist/commands/auth.js      (src/commands/auth.ts)
showcase  → dist/commands/showcase.js  (src/commands/showcase.ts)
```

### Atomic Writes

Every file write follows this pattern to prevent partial writes from crash
or power loss:

```
1. Write content to <target-path>.tmp  (atomic write via writeFile)
2. fs.rename(<target-path>.tmp, <target-path>)  (atomic rename)
```

`fs.rename` is atomic on the same filesystem — the `.tmp` file and the
target are guaranteed to be on the same filesystem since they share the
same directory. On Windows, `fs.rename` requires that the target does not
exist (we unlink it first), or we use `fs.copyFile` + `fs.unlink` as
fallback.

### Backup Manager

Backups are stored at `~/.claude/hawiyat-backups/` with the naming pattern:

```
<original-basename>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.json
```

Examples: `settings-20260601-120000.json`, `opencode-20260601-120000.json`.

**Behavior:**
- A backup is created before every write to a managed file
- Each backup is SHA256-hashed on creation; the hash is recorded in the
  manifest
- On restore, the backup file's hash is verified before writing
- Up to 5 backups per original file are retained (oldest pruned)
- Pruning is soft — never delete backups on uninstall (user may need to
  rollback after uninstall)

### Manifest

The manifest at `~/.claude/hawiyat-manifest.json` tracks installation
state, backup history, and plugin ownership:

```json
{
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "installDate": "2026-06-01T12:00:00.000Z",
  "lastUpdateDate": "2026-06-01T12:00:00.000Z",
  "installInProgress": false,
  "hawiyatCliVersion": "1.0.0",
  "files": {
    "/home/user/.claude/settings.json": {
      "currentSha256": "abc123...",
      "lastBackup": "/home/user/.claude/hawiyat-backups/settings-20260601-120000.json",
      "backupHistory": [...]
    }
  },
  "plugins": [...],
  "envOverrides": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://ai.hawiyat.cloud",
    "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "sk-Hxr7...CUBg",
    "ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "hawiyat-composer"
  }
}
```

All paths in the manifest are absolute resolved paths (via `path.resolve`)
— never tilde-prefixed — to work correctly across different environments
(WSL vs native Windows).

### Merge Engine

The `smartInject` function merges new Hawiyat values into an existing
configuration object while preserving all user customizations:

1. Deep-clone the target (via `structuredClone`)
2. For top-level keys not `env`: set only if the key is absent from target
3. For the `env` block: overwrite only keys in `managedKeys`
   (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`,
   `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY`)
4. Preserve all other `env` keys (`HTTP_PROXY`, custom vars, etc.)

Conflict detection is separate: if a managed key exists with a different
value, the installer warns and prompts for confirmation (or respects
`--force`).

### Token Priority

```
1. --token CLI flag
2. ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN environment variable
3. ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN stored in the target settings.json
   (written by `hawiyat auth login`)
4. Interactive prompt (node:readline, silent echo)
```

If no token is resolved after all four, the installer exits with code 2.
The stored value is what lets `hawiyat auth login` run once and every later
`install` reuse the key without `--token`.
The token is masked in output (first 4 + last 4 characters) and is never
passed to subprocesses.

### Plugin Install

When `--full` is used, the installer writes the `superpowers` plugin entry
into `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` directly (rather than
calling `claude plugins install` as a subprocess).

**Verified format (Claude Code v2.1.159):**

```json
{
  "installedPlugins": [
    {
      "marketplaceIdentifier": "superpowers@claude-plugins-official",
      "version": "5.1.0",
      "installDate": "2026-06-01T12:00:00.000Z",
      "source": {
        "type": "marketplace",
        "marketplaceIdentifier": "claude-plugins-official"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> Verified against Claude Code v2.1.159. Format may change in future
> versions — if a fallback to `claude plugins install` subprocess should
> be implemented, the format would need re-verification.

**Ownership tracking:** The manifest records which plugins were installed
by Hawiyat. On uninstall, only plugins with `installedByHawiyat: true` and
matching version are removed.

## Install Command Flow

> **Codex-only branch (`--codex`):** When `--codex` is passed, the install
> flow diverges immediately after token resolution — it skips the Claude
> `settings.json`, OpenCode, and plugin steps entirely. Instead it writes
> `~/.codex/config.toml` (full hawiyat provider block plus
> `[projects."<path>"]` trust when `--project` is set) and
> `~/.codex/auth.json` (`auth_mode: "apikey"`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`). With
> `--project`, a project-local `.codex/config.toml` containing only `model`
> is also written (Codex denylists provider keys there). The model picker is
> populated through `model_catalog_json`: model ids come from `--models`,
> gateway discovery (`GET {base_url}/v1/models`, best-effort), the existing
> catalog file, or a static fallback list, and the catalog JSON is written to
> `~/.codex/hawiyat-model-catalog.json`. Non-`hawiyat-` models known to be
> Hawiyat-served (currently `gpt-image-2.5` and `gpt-image-2`) are allowlisted into the catalog
> so they survive discovery filtering. The same
> backup/manifest/idempotency (exit 5) semantics apply.
>
> The install also writes a `hawiyat-imagegen` skill to
> `~/.codex/skills/hawiyat-imagegen/` (`SKILL.md` + dependency-free node
> runner) that routes image generate/edit requests through the gateway's
> Images API. The skill defaults to `gpt-image-2.5` and still offers
> `gpt-image-2` via `--model`. `update` refreshes the skill files; `uninstall --purge`
> removes the skill dir alongside the catalog.
>
> **Harness targets (`--targets`, `--pi`, `--deepseek`, `--interactive`):**
> Selecting pi, DeepSeek Harness, any `--targets` list, or the interactive
> wizard routes to `install-harnesses.ts`. That module owns one lock /
> manifest / telemetry cycle, resolves the token and model list once
> (explicit `--models` > `discoverGatewayModelIds()` > `hawiyat-composer`,
> `hawiyat-astra`), then writes each selected harness:
>
> - `claude` → `writeSettingsWithDefaults()` (`~/.claude/settings.json`)
> - `opencode` → `mergeOpencodeConfig()` with `versionMajor` parsed from
>   `opencode --version` (V1 `provider` for 1.x, V2 `providers` for 2.x)
> - `pi` → `writePiConfig()` (`~/.pi/agent/models.json`, `auth.json`, and
>   `settings.json` when Hawiyat is the default)
> - `deepseek` → `writeDeepseekConfig()` (`cordis.patch.yml` + `.env`)
>
> After the OpenCode write it runs `opencode models` best-effort and warns
> about the known OpenCode 2.x custom-provider bug when `hawiyat` is absent.
> The default install path (no target flags, `claude,opencode`) is unchanged.
> `--targets` / `--pi` / `--deepseek` / `--interactive` cannot be combined
> with the exclusive `--codex*` / `--claude-desktop` flags (exit 2).
>
> **Claude Desktop branch (`--claude-desktop`):** Claude Desktop (Chat,
> Cowork, Code) ignores `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and `~/.claude/settings.json`
> for routing, and `claude_desktop_config.json` only registers MCP servers.
> The CLI instead writes `~/.claude/hawiyat-claude-desktop.json` with
> `inferenceProvider: "gateway"`, the gateway URL/key, bearer auth, and
> `inferenceModels`; the user imports it once via Help > Troubleshooting >
> Enable Developer Mode > Developer > Configure Third-Party Inference.
> A managed configuration (Admin Console, macOS profile, Windows
> `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude`, Linux
> `/etc/claude-desktop/managed-settings.json`) wins and makes the in-app
> form read-only. The encrypted `configLibrary/` directory is never written.

  └─12. LOG summary → EXIT 0

## Security Model

1. **Token in settings.json only** — never in shell rc, never in logs,
   never passed to subprocesses.
2. **File permissions** — `0o600` on Linux/macOS after write (owner
   read/write only).
3. **Masked output** — tokens shown as `sk-Hxr7…CUBg` (first 4 + last 4).
4. **No postinstall hooks** — zero npm install scripts.
5. **Telemetry** — one PostHog event per mutating command (platform, Node
   version, token SHA-256, install ID). `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` disables it;
   `HAWIYAT_TELEMETRY_HOST` overrides the host.
6. **Atomic writes** — no partial/corrupt files.
7. **SHA256 verification** — backups and restores are integrity-checked.

## Cross-Platform

| Concern                 | Solution                                              |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| Home directory          | `os.homedir()` — same API on macOS, Linux, Windows    |
| File permissions        | `fs.chmod(0o600)` — Linux/macOS only (no-op on Win)   |
| Path separators         | `path.join()` — handles `/` and `\`                   |
| Plugin install          | Direct `installed_plugins.json` write (no subprocess) |
| Terminal interaction    | `node:readline/promises` — works on all platforms     |
| Unsafe `fs.rename`      | Windows requires unlink before rename; detect via EEXIST |
| Colors in output        | ANSI codes auto-disabled when `!process.stdout.isTTY` or `NO_COLOR` is set |

# Releasing

A release is one tag. The tag publishes two npm names and creates a GitHub
release:

| Name | Role |
|---|---|
| `@hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude` | the core package, source of truth |
| `hawiyat` | alias, exact-pinned to the core version, no code of its own |

`-rc.N` versions publish to the npm `next` dist-tag. A stable version moves
`latest`. The publish workflow refuses a tag that does not equal
`v$(package.json version)`.

## One-time setup: trusted publishing

The workflow has no npm token. npm trusts the GitHub workflow through OIDC.
Requirements: npm >= 11.5.1, Node >= 22.14, GitHub-hosted runners. The workflow
upgrades npm itself.

For **each** package on npmjs.com, open the package → **Settings** →
**Trusted Publisher** → **GitHub Actions** and enter:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Organization or user | `Hawiyat-Org` |
| Repository | `hawiyat-kit` |
| Workflow filename | `publish.yml` |
| Environment name | leave empty |
| Allowed actions | allow `npm publish`; allow `npm dist-tag` if this workflow will move tags |

The fields are case-sensitive and checked only at publish time. A new
configuration must complete its first publish within two days or it expires.

`hawiyat` must exist before its settings page exists. Create it once, by hand,
with 2FA:

```bash
cd packages/hawiyat && npm publish --access public --tag next
```

or stage it and approve it on npmjs.com:

```bash
npm stage publish
```

After both packages have published once through OIDC, open **Settings** →
**Publishing access** and choose **Require two-factor authentication and
disallow tokens**. Revoke the old `NPM_TOKEN` and delete the repository secret.

## Cut a release

```bash
node scripts/sync-alias.mjs          # after bumping the root version
npm test && node test/integration-test.mjs
git commit -am "release: 1.6.7-rc.1"
git tag -a v1.6.7-rc.1 -m "v1.6.7-rc.1"
git push origin main
git push origin v1.6.7-rc.1
```

The workflow then:

1. checks the tag against `package.json`;
2. installs with `npm ci` and runs the unit tests;
3. publishes the core package (`prepublishOnly` reruns build, unit and
   integration tests), skipping a version already on npm;
4. syncs the alias and publishes it the same way;
5. creates the GitHub release, marked prerelease for a `-rc` tag.

## Promote

Once the dashboard on production serves the device and desktop routes:

```bash
npm dist-tag add @hawiyat-team/hawiyat-claude@1.6.7 latest
npm dist-tag add hawiyat@1.6.7 latest
```

This needs npm >= 11.21.0 and **Allow npm dist-tag** on the trusted publisher.

## Roll back

A published version cannot be unpublished safely, and a moved `latest` should
not move backwards. Fix forward with a new patch version, then move `latest`.

## Problem
`hawiyat-claude install` needs a key from `--token`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or a prompt (`src/core/token.ts:21-33`). The key comes from the dashboard, which is session-gated, so every install starts with a copy from a browser. Goal: `hawiyat auth login` authorizes this machine from any terminal, including SSH, and writes the key through the existing settings path. The plan key never travels in a URL.

## Verified current state
Dashboard (Next.js App Router, Node runtime):

- Session is a JWT cookie `session`, HS256, 7 day max age, `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax` (`src/lib/auth.ts:6-7`, `:34`, `:80`). `getSessionFromRequest()` is the read path (`:91-95`).
- Google login builds its own URL and a 600 s state cookie (`src/app/api/auth/google/route.ts:7`, `:41-51`); the callback verifies state, creates the session, sets the cookie (`src/app/api/auth/google/callback/route.ts:46-57`, `:149`, `:190`). There is no `next` support today.
- `GET /api/tokens/list` is the only raw-key route: it blocks impersonation, rate limits per email, sends `no-store` (`src/app/api/tokens/list/route.ts:22-24`, `:26-28`, `:37-48`). Keys come from a KV cache, not from a creation call (`src/lib/types.ts:231-235`, `:237-248`).
- `GET /api/keys` is mask-only by contract (`src/app/api/keys/route.ts:13-26`, `:71-75`). Plan comes from `metadata.tier` through `derivePlan()` (`src/lib/cost.ts:120-131`, `src/app/api/keys/route.ts:40`).
- Durable state is SQLite with migrations in `migrations/`, newest `0020_renewal_payment.sql`. KV takes a TTL (`src/lib/kv.ts:57`, `:74`, `:90`) but cannot make a check-then-consume atomic. ## Decision
RFC 8628 Device Authorization Grant, owned by the dashboard. The CLI asks for a device code, the user approves it in a browser under the existing Google session, and the dashboard mints a per-device, plan-limited, revocable key that only the polling token call can collect. It works over SSH, in containers, and on hosts that cannot accept a local listener.
Loopback Authorization Code + PKCE S256 stays as an optional `--loopback` path.
Rejected: loopback as default (needs a listenable port, fails over SSH and under strict egress); deep link to the Keys page (consent becomes a click with no CSRF contract); handing out the existing plan key (one leak forces plan-wide rotation, while a device key is revoked alone by `blockKey()`).

### 1. Discovery
`GET https://dash.hawiyat.cloud/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`

```json
{"issuer":"https://dash.hawiyat.cloud",
 "device_authorization_endpoint":"https://dash.hawiyat.cloud/api/cli/device_authorization",
 "token_endpoint":"https://dash.hawiyat.cloud/api/cli/token",
 "revocation_endpoint":"https://dash.hawiyat.cloud/api/cli/revoke",
 "grant_types_supported":["urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code","authorization_code"],
 "response_types_supported":["code"],"code_challenge_methods_supported":["S256"],
 "token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported":["none"]}
```
Static JSON, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`, no user data.

### 2. Device authorization
`POST /api/cli/device_authorization`, form-encoded `client_id=hawiyat-cli` and optional `device_name`.

- Reject any other `client_id`. The `device_code` is 32 random bytes, base64url, stored only as `sha256`; the `user_code` is 8 characters from Crockford base32 `0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ` (40 bits, `I`/`L` fold to `1`, `O` to `0` on input), shown as `ABCD-EFGH`, stored only as `sha256(normalized)`.
- Insert one row in a new `cli_grants` table (migration `0021_*.sql`): `flow='device'`, `status='pending'`, `expires_at = now + 600`, `interval_seconds = 5`, sanitized `device_name`.
- Respond `no-store`:

```json
{"device_code":"...","user_code":"ABCD-EFGH",
 "verification_uri":"https://dash.hawiyat.cloud/device",
 "verification_uri_complete":"https://dash.hawiyat.cloud/device?code=ABCD-EFGH",
 "expires_in":600,"interval":5}
```

Rate limit 5 starts per minute per IP. The user code is not a secret and grants nothing on its own.

### 3. Device page
`GET /device` at `src/app/device/page.tsx`, outside `[lang]`, so the printed URL needs no locale prefix.

- Code form, uppercase, hyphen optional, input normalised to the alphabet before lookup. Unknown, expired, or already used code: one message, no distinction, because distinguishing them is an oracle.
- No session: redirect to `/api/auth/google?next=/device?code=<code>`. This needs the new `next` support in the Google route, allowlisting only `/device` and `/api/cli/` paths.
- Pending code: consent view naming the requesting `device_name` (from the grant row, sanitized, length capped) and the signed-in email, stating that approval mints a key for that machine. Approve and Deny post to the routes below.
- Session plus impersonation: refuse. Approval is a customer action, matching the raw-key rule at `src/app/api/tokens/list/route.ts:22-24`.

### 4. Approve and deny
`POST /api/cli/device/approve` and `POST /api/cli/device/deny`, form-encoded `user_code` plus a CSRF token.

- Require session, `isAllowedOriginStrict` (`src/lib/api-utils.ts:52-55`), and a CSRF token bound to the session subject. `SameSite=Lax` alone is not enough for a POST that mints a key. The `user_code` hash is compared in constant time before the row is touched.
- Approve is one conditional UPDATE: `SET status='approved', user_email=?, approved_at=? WHERE user_code_hash=? AND status='pending' AND expires_at>?`, requiring exactly one row. A second approval of the same code changes nothing. Deny is the same shape with `status='denied'`.
- Rate limit 5 approvals per minute per IP and per code hash. Respond with a plain confirmation page that never echoes the device code.

### 5. Token
`POST /api/cli/token`, form-encoded.

Device grant: `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`, `device_code`, `client_id=hawiyat-cli`.

| State of the grant | Status | Body |
|---|---|---|
| pending | 400 | `{"error":"authorization_pending"}` |
| polled faster than `interval` | 400 | `{"error":"slow_down"}` |
| denied | 400 | `{"error":"access_denied"}` |
| past `expires_at` | 400 | `{"error":"expired_token"}` |
| approved, first poll | 200 | `{"access_token":"sk-...","token_type":"Bearer","expires_in":7776000,"key_alias":"cli-laptop-20261111"}` |

- Every response is `no-store`. Unknown `device_code` returns `expired_token`, not 404, so a probe learns nothing.
- Consume with one conditional UPDATE: `SET status='consumed', used_at=? WHERE device_code_hash=? AND status='approved' AND used_at IS NULL`. Zero rows changed means another poll won the race, so return `expired_token`. Polling is capped at 60 per `device_code` so a loop cannot hammer the proxy.
- Mint after the row is claimed, with `POST /key/generate` and the master key: alias `cli-<hostname>-<YYYYMMDD>`, `user_id` = the approving email, `duration` 90d, `models` from that plan tier, `metadata.source = "hawiyat-cli"`. If minting fails, flip the row back to `approved` so the client can retry, and return 502.

Authorization Code grant, `--loopback` only: shipped as `GET /api/cli/authorize` and `POST /api/cli/consent` in the same change, behind the same flag. `code`, `code_verifier`, `redirect_uri` are checked against the same `cli_grants` row (`flow='code'`, `sha256(code)`, 60 s TTL, exact redirect and `client_id` match, constant-time PKCE compare) before the same mint call.

### 6. Revoke
`POST /api/cli/revoke` with `{"key_alias":"..."}`. Require a session, resolve the alias through that email's token cache, call `blockKey()` (`src/lib/litellm.ts:149-166`), return 204. Another user's alias returns 404, not 403. Reuse block over a new `/key/delete`: it is already the Keys page action and is reversible.

## CLI behavior
`hawiyat auth login` (default device flow):

1. `POST /api/cli/device_authorization` with the sanitized hostname as `device_name` and a 15 s timeout.
2. Print exactly:

```
$ hawiyat auth login

Open this URL in your browser:
https://dash.hawiyat.cloud/device

Enter this code:
ABCD-EFGH

Waiting for authorization...
```

3. Poll `POST /api/cli/token` with the device grant at the returned `interval` (5 s), each poll with a 10 s timeout. On `slow_down`, add 5 s to the interval. Stop at `expires_in` (600 s) or after 60 polls.
4. On `access_denied` or `expired_token`, print one line naming the reason and exit 4.
5. On 200, write `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY` through `writeSettingsWithDefaults()` (`src/core/settings.ts:112-134`), so backup, atomic write, manifest, and `0600` match install exactly. Print the alias and the token masked by `maskToken()` (`src/core/token.ts:13-19`).

Flags: `--open` also launches the browser (macOS `open`, Windows `cmd /c start "" <url>`, Linux `xdg-open`); `--loopback` selects Authorization Code + PKCE on `127.0.0.1:0`, 120 s wait; `--alias <name>` overrides the generated alias; `--no-browser` is accepted in loopback mode only. `auth status` reads the local settings and prints alias, plan, expiry, and masked token, or "not logged in". `auth logout` clears the managed env keys; `--revoke` calls `/api/cli/revoke` first.

Exit codes: 0 key written; 1 generic, network or mint failure; 2 invalid input or bad arguments; 3 permission denied writing settings; 4 authorization denied or expired; 5 already configured without `--force`. Codes 1, 2, 3, and 5 match `src/utils/exit.ts:3-12`; 4 takes over the `PARTIAL_FAILURE` slot, which no other command returns for this path.

## Threat model
| Risk | Control |
|---|---|
| User-code phishing (main risk) | 10 minute TTL, one-time use, approval needs an authenticated session, consent page names the device and the email, rate limits per IP and per code |
| Code guessing | 40 bits of code, 5 attempts per minute per IP, single message for unknown/expired/used |
| Key in the wrong hands | No key in the code, key only in the token response body over TLS, `no-store`, `0600` on disk |
| Stolen laptop | Per-device key, plan models, 90 day expiry, revocable from Keys or `auth logout --revoke` |
| Cross-user approval | `user_email` comes from the session, never from the request; token grant reads it from the row |
| Replay of an approved grant | Conditional UPDATE to `consumed`; a second poll gets `expired_token` |
| Redirect binding | Weaker than loopback PKCE, which is the reason `--loopback` stays available |

## Tests
Dashboard:

- Device code format is 8 alphabet characters, displayed `ABCD-EFGH`, and only hashes are stored.

- Polling state machine: `authorization_pending`, then `slow_down` when faster than the interval, then 200 after approval.
